summary: Petition under Section 79, including Section 79 (1)(c), 79 (1)(f) and 79 (1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003, seeking direction upon the Respondents to allow the said Petitioner to convert and continue its old connectivity under the new regime without the need of applying for GNA. The Petitioner, Bharat Aluminium Company Ltd. (BALCO), has filed the instant Petition under Section 79, 79 (1)(c), 79 (1)(f) and 79 (1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to ‘the Act’), seeking direction upon the Respondents to convert and continue its old connectivity under the new regime without the need of applying for mandatory GNA. 2. The Petitioner has also filed an IA No. 83/2023 seeking an amendment to the Petition. The IA was allowed by the Commission vide RoP of hearing dated 14.02.2024. Accordingly, the Petitioner amended the Petition. The Petitioner has made the following prayers in the amended Petition: _(d) Pass any other orders, as this commission may deem fit and proper in the light of the facts and circumstances of the instant case.”_ - i) It is the case of the Petitioner that the Petitioner is already connected with the ISTS, and as such, it does not require to mandatorily apply for the GNA. Accordingly, the provisions of 17.1(iii) will not apply in the case of the Petitioner. As such, the Petitioner, - n) Subsequently, the Commission vide order dated 22.09.2023 in Petition No. 11/SM/2023, clarified the above position as under: - w) The present case is a fit case for the Commission to exercise its powers under Regulation 41, viz. “Power to relax”. Additionally, the Commission can also invoke its powers to remove difficulties provided under Regulation 42 in order to grant relief in the present Petition. The Commission has the necessary jurisdiction under Section 79 of the Act, including under Section 79(1)(c), which provides the Commission with power to regulate inter-State transmission of electricity. 4. The Petition was admitted, and notice was issued to the parties to file their respective replies. 5. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner reiterated the submissions made in the Petition. After hearing the parties, the Commission, vide RoP for the hearing dated 29.09.2023, granted interim relief and observed as under: - f) CERC vide order dated 22.09.2023 in Petition No. 11/SM/2023 regarding removal of difficulties under various provisions of the GNA Regulations allowed the inclusion of transition of Regulation17.1(iii) entities whose Connectivity is effective under Regulation 37.6(1) of the GNA Regulations. 7. During the course of the hearing dated 14.02.2024 the Commission directed that the amended Petition be taken on the record and directed the Respondent, CTUIL, to file its reply on the amended Petition. c) In furtherance to interim Order passed by Commission during hearing held on 29.9.2023 and in response to the email dated 25.9.2023 of Respondent No.1, the Petitioner vide its email dated 10.1.2024 requested Respondent No.1 to defer the processing of the application of the Petitioner for the grant of 200MW GNARE, on account of the issue concerning the drawal of power through the T-GNA or GNA under the GNA Regulations for a Bulk consumer being sub-judice before this Commission and the interim Order dated 29.9.2023 passed therein. 9. The Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 10.04.2024, has filed its rejoinder to the reply filed by CTUIL on 28.02.2024 by reiterating its earlier submissions and has additionally submitted as below: 13. The Petitioner, vide Written Submission dated 07.08.2024, has reiterated its earlier submissions and has additionally submitted as under: a) Both of the Petitioner’s entity works on the principle of displacement of power, which not only ensures the stability of the grid but also lessens the actual usage of the transmission corridor. This is illustrated with the following two examples: 16. The Petitioner, vide written submission dated 25.09.2024, reiterated its earlier submissions and has additionally submitted as follows: g) After recognizing the problems and issues being faced by the Bulk consumers, the Commission may initiate steps for amending the GNA Regulations to give relief to Bulk consumers so that they are not required/ forced/ compelled to take mandatory GNA equal to their connectivity. Till such an amendment takes place, the interim order dated 29.09.2023 granted by this Commission ought to continue. 17. After hearing the parties at length, the Commission reserved the matter for order, and the parties were permitted to file their brief note of arguments. 21. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and the Respondents. The following issues arise for our consideration: Order in Petition No. 192/MP/2023 28. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and the Respondents. Let us peruse the regulatory provisions. 31. The relevant extract of the Commission’s Order dated 22.09.2023 in Petition No. “ _41. The Central Commission, for reasons to be recorded in writing, may relax any of the provisions of these regulations on its own motion or on an application made before it by an affected party to remove the hardship arising out of the operation of these regulations.”_ “ _ 18.1 The Regulations of the Central Commission and the decision of the Tribunal and the Supreme Court confer the judicial discretion to the Central Commission to exercise power to relax in exceptional case. However, while exercising the power to relax there -_ _ should be sufficient reason to justify the relaxation and non exercise of discretion would cause hardship and injustice to a party or lead to unjust result. It has also to be established by the party that the circumstances are not created due to act of omission or commission attributable to the party claiming relaxation. Further, the reasons justifying relaxation have to be recorded in writing.” _
title: Petition under Section 79, including Section 79 (1)(c), 79 (1)(f) and 79 (1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003, seeking direction upon the Respondents to allow the said Petitioner to convert and continue its old connectivity under the new regime without the need of applying for GNA.
